record_verbatim.objective: Confirm that a hostile peer cannot make the service unavailable to a legitimate peer by opening the maximum number of permitted connections and sending nothing on them, and that every refusal and every budget breach is diagnosable. This is the measure for the requirement's availability clause; the resource figures it checks are the requirement's own, not figures this measure chooses.

oracle_detail.model_sensitivity: Availability under exhaustion falls as C rises. At C = 4 with a 2000 ms timeout the worst case is that 4 of the pool are blocked for at most 2 s each. Raising C to 16 without shortening T would make a silent peer able to consume four times the blocked-time budget, which is why the requirement fixes both figures rather than one.
oracle_detail.what_it_still_does_not_prove: The model says nothing about a peer that stays within the caps and still consumes the service's CPU through a cheap request pattern, nor about a peer that opens and closes rapidly enough to churn through the cap. It also cannot prove the 'resources released' part of the breach criterion, which is a code-path property no external model reaches.
oracle_detail.what_the_oracle_is_not: It is not a measurement: no service was starved and nothing was timed. It is not a source-grounded oracle: the caps are engineering choices, not properties of a protocol, and the requirement carries them as proposals. It is not a synthetic assumption about the world, though it is an assumption about the implementation: the model holds only if the implementation actually enforces the caps rather than declaring them.
oracle_detail.why_this_oracle: The oracle is a resource model rather than an observation. A service with a hard cap C on concurrent connections and a finite receive timeout T cannot be starved by a peer that sends nothing: at most C connections can be blocked for at most T each, after which their resources are reclaimed, so the steady-state availability of the remaining capacity is a function of C and T and not of how long the hostile peer holds its sockets. The expected outcomes are the model's outputs - C, T, the byte budget and the breach-response time - each chosen so the model closes: 4 connections at a 2000 ms timeout bounds the blocked-time budget, and a 128 KiB burst exceeds the 65536-byte budget by a factor of two so the breach is unambiguous.

preconditions: The service under test implements the caps the requirement states.
The hostile peer can hold sockets open without sending data.
The legitimate peer behaves as a legitimate peer.
record_verbatim.regression_selection: Re-run on any change to the connection limit, the timeout, the buffer sizes or the accept loop. This is the measure that would catch the single-deep-queue and discarded-enqueue behaviour the requirement's rationale describes, so it is never sampled out.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.

Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
